question: What is the primary purpose of musculoskeletal adaptations during pregnancy?

options.B: To accommodate the growing fetus and prepare for birth
options.C: To increase maternal bone mineral density permanently
options.D: To prevent all forms of gestational weight gain

explanation: Musculoskeletal adaptations occur primarily to accommodate the growing fetus and successfully prepare the maternal body for labor and delivery. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h1)

question: Why is it important for nursing students to understand these musculoskeletal changes?

options.A: To prescribe heavy weightlifting routines for pregnant women
options.B: To differentiate normal discomforts from pathological conditions
options.C: To prevent the natural hormonal surges of pregnancy
options.D: To eliminate the need for postpartum assessments

explanation: Understanding normal physiological adaptations allows nurses to accurately differentiate between expected pregnancy discomforts and true pathological conditions. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h1)

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for collagen remodeling and widespread connective tissue relaxation during pregnancy?
explanation: Relaxin is the key hormone produced during pregnancy that remodels collagen and promotes connective tissue and joint laxity. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h2)

question: What is a major clinical consequence of systemic joint laxity in pregnant women?

options.A: Increased risk of joint sprains and strains
options.B: Permanent hardening of the spinal column
options.D: Enhanced bone density in weight-bearing joints

explanation: Generalized joint laxity decreases joint stability, placing pregnant women at a higher risk for sprains, strains, and accidental injuries. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h2)

question: In which direction does the maternal center of gravity shift as the pregnancy progresses?
explanation: The growing uterus causes the maternal center of gravity to shift forward and upward, forcing compensatory postural changes. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h3)

question: What type of footwear should nurses recommend to help mitigate postural instability during pregnancy?
explanation: Flat, supportive shoes help provide a stable base of support and prevent exacerbating the forward center of gravity shift caused by heels. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h3)

question: What term describes the exaggerated inward curvature of the lumbar spine seen in pregnant women?
explanation: Gestational lordosis is the characteristic exaggerated inward curvature of the lower back that develops to compensate for the forward shift in weight. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h4)

question: Which of the following contributes significantly to pregnancy-related back pain alongside mechanical strain?

options.A: Separation of the rectus abdominis muscles
options.B: Excessive strengthening of the core muscles
options.C: Complete rigidity of the pelvic ligaments

explanation: The separation of the rectus abdominis muscles (diastasis recti) weakens core support for the spine, worsening back pain during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h4)

question: What causes the severe discomfort associated with Symphysis Pubis Dysfunction (SPD)?

options.A: Excessive and asymmetrical mobility of the pelvic joints
options.B: Complete fusion of the pubic symphysis bone

explanation: SPD occurs when the pelvic joints become excessively or asymmetrically mobile, leading to localized pain and instability. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h5)

question: Which nursing advice is most appropriate for a pregnant client experiencing Symphysis Pubis Dysfunction?

options.A: Stand on one leg while dressing
options.B: Keep knees together when getting out of bed
options.D: Avoid wearing any form of pelvic support

explanation: Keeping the knees together when transitioning movements helps minimize stress on the unstable pubic symphysis joint. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h5)

question: What is the primary cause of dependent lower extremity edema in late pregnancy?

options.B: Compression of the inferior vena cava by the gravid uterus

explanation: The heavy, gravid uterus compresses the inferior vena cava, increasing venous pressure and causing fluid to pool in the lower extremities. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h6)

question: Which intervention can a nurse recommend to help relieve nocturnal leg cramps in pregnancy?
explanation: Performing gentle calf stretches before bedtime helps relax the muscle fibers and reduce the frequency of painful nocturnal cramps. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h6)

question: How does the coccyx adapt to facilitate the passage of the fetal head during delivery?

options.B: It pivots backward because it is mobile
options.C: It locks rigidly into a fixed anterior position
options.D: It detaches completely from the sacrum

explanation: The mobile coccyx pivots backward during delivery to help expand the pelvic outlet for the passing fetus. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h7)

question: Which maternal labor position helps maximize pelvic outlet diameters and utilizes gravity?
explanation: Upright positions and squatting maximize pelvic dimensions and use gravity to help the fetus descend efficiently. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h7)

question: What hormonal shift triggers the beginning of musculoskeletal recovery and the return of joint stability postpartum?

options.A: A sharp drop in relaxin and progesterone levels
options.B: A massive surge in placental hormone production
options.C: A permanent cessation of estrogen synthesis
options.D: An increase in fetal growth hormone

explanation: The rapid drop in relaxin and progesterone levels after delivery initiates the involution and tightening of ligaments and joints. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h8)

question: Why are postpartum women still at risk for musculoskeletal injuries shortly after birth?

options.A: Their bones instantly become fragile and brittle
options.B: Joint laxity can persist for several weeks postpartum
options.C: Relaxin levels remain permanently elevated for life
options.D: They are required to perform heavy weightlifting

explanation: Because joint laxity persists for weeks after delivery, new mothers remain at risk for strain while handling infant care tasks. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h8)

question: What is the primary focus of management for pregnancy-related musculoskeletal discomforts?

options.C: Complete bed rest for the entire pregnancy

explanation: Management emphasizes non-pharmacological approaches, patient education on ergonomics, lifestyle modifications, and comfort measures. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h9)

question: When should a nurse refer a pregnant client experiencing musculoskeletal pain to a specialist or physician?

options.A: When she reports mild, expected postural fatigue
options.B: When pain becomes severe, incapacitating, or shows signs of nerve impingement
options.C: Before any antenatal education takes place
options.D: Whenever she wears flat supportive shoes

explanation: Severe, disabling pain or signs of nerve impingement like sciatica require formal referral for specialized physical therapy or medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h9)
